newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. tries to get Israel and Syria to talk peace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tries to get Israel and Syria to talk peace.

text.p: The United States is trying to get Israel and Syria to revive peace talks suspended 10 months ago, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday.

U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk told reporters in PLO-ruled Gaza: "This is something that we will be working on in the months ahead -- to try to get the Israeli-Syrian and the Israeli-Lebanese negotiations back on track".
Netanyahu told reporters in Haifa, northern Israel, he was certain Israel and Syria would find a "bridging formula" to restart the U.S.-brokered peace talks.
His refusal to hand back the Golan Heights -- a strategic plateau captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war -- has raised Syrian suspicions he is not committed to peace.

"There are contacts through the United States and attempts through the United States to renew the negotiations and there are areas on which there is potential agreement," said the Israeli leader, who took office last June.
Syria demands the return of the Golan Heights. Israel broke off talks launched with Syria in 1991 after a series of Islamist suicide bombings in Israel last February and March.
"There are many areas on which there is no agreement and one of them is the Golan," Netanyahu said. "It in the end we will find the way to renew the negotiations and complete them."
